title: A Echo for the Signal Revisited
premise: Odile Brightwater, a clone created to inherit his original's unsolved murder investigation, arrives at Meridian Deep expecting a quiet records audit and instead finds a dying colony whose children share an identical dream of fire. As he digs into the erased massacre that killed his original, he falls for colony medic Sefa Anand and bonds with the forgotten community she refuses to abandon. When the corporation sends a cleanup fleet to erase the last witnesses, Odile must choose between the duty encoded in his blood and the family he never expected. He broadcasts the children's shared memory as living testimony, dooming himself to deletion but forcing justice outside any court—and Sefa smuggles his consciousness out in the signal itself.
about_author: Wren Ravensworth is the pen name of a former radio archivist who spent a decade cataloguing dead frequencies and the voices trapped inside them. They write science fiction about people the future tried to forget.

chapters.title: The Inheritance Clause
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. He wakes in a cloning vat with his original's memories and one unfinished case: a murder on Meridian Deep, a colony officially listed as thriving. Arriving by supply skimmer, he finds rusted domes and half-empty streets. The emotional beat is quiet unease—the paperwork says paradise, but the air smells like ash nobody will discuss.

chapters.title: Children of the Same Dream
chapters.summary: Odile's POV, shifting briefly to nine-year-old Tam Voss. The colony's remaining children all describe the same recurring dream: a corridor filling with orange light and screaming. Their parents go pale and change the subject. Odile realizes the dream matches coordinates in his original's final notes. The beat is dread disguised as curiosity.

chapters.title: Sefa Keeps the Lights On
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. The colony medic patches failing life support with scavenged parts and treats Odile's frostbitten hands after he collapses surveying the sealed east wing. She's sharp, exhausted, and fiercely protective of the kids. She warns him off the east wing. The beat is warmth kindling against her better judgment—two caretakers recognizing each other.

chapters.title: Records That Lie Beautifully
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. He decrypts his original's hidden cache: shipping manifests showing four hundred colonists arrived, census logs listing ninety-one. Every official record has been retroactively edited from corporate headquarters. His original died asking why. The beat is cold fury—Odile understands for the first time that he was made to be disposable too.

chapters.title: What the East Wing Remembers
chapters.summary: Odile and Sefa's alternating POV. They breach the sealed wing together and find scorch patterns, a mass grave site paved over, and a child's shoe fused to the floor. Sefa finally admits she survived something she can't speak about. The beat is grief breaking open; intimacy forged in horror rather than comfort.

chapters.title: The Company Sends Flowers
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. A corporate liaison arrives with supplies, praise, and a quiet offer: close the file, take a promotion, forget. That night someone ransacks his quarters and steals the manifest copies. Tam goes missing. The beat is escalating menace—the colony's invisibility was always protection, and Odile has stripped it away.

chapters.title: Tam's Testimony
chapters.summary: Tam's POV, then Odile's. Found hiding in the old comms tower, Tam reveals the dreams aren't dreams—they're inherited memory, passed between the children like a signal, replaying the massacre night. The children are the only unedited records left. The beat is terrible hope: the truth exists, but only in minds the company considers worthless.

chapters.title: Duty Is a Loaded Word
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The cleanup fleet enters orbit with orders to sterilize the colony as a 'biohazard event.' Odile's own genetic contract activates—he's legally company property, compelled to assist the erasure. Sefa asks him to run with them. The beat is heartbreak at the crossroads: love against duty, and duty has guns.

chapters.title: Broadcast the Dead
chapters.summary: Odile, Sefa, and Tam's POV braided together. In the comms tower they splice the children's shared memory into a colony-wide broadcast aimed at every relay in the system—the massacre as lived testimony no edit can touch. The fleet opens fire on the tower. The beat is defiant climax: making the invisible impossible to unsee, whatever it costs.

chapters.title: A Echo for the Signal Revisited
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV, months later. The broadcast worked; inquiries begin, the fleet recalled, the company exposed. Odile's body didn't survive the tower, but Sefa carries his backed-up consciousness in an old radio, teaching the children to rebuild. Sometimes the signal hums a tune only he knew. The beat is bittersweet resolution—justice won, family kept, love outlasting the body that held it.
